browserPolicy: New isolated headless Chrome process and temporary profile; localhost:4207 only; no existing Chrome or CDP port connection.
runtimePolicy: No application-state injection, runtime edits, forced animation completion or synthetic DOM scroll. Desktop motion uses browser wheel input followed by supported ArrowUp/ArrowDown keys to stop native tunnel auto-scroll and settle near the target; touch uses Input.dispatchTouchEvent on this harness-owned page.
externalPolicy: All non-local HTTP(S) requests are blocked and recorded. Vimeo playback and external links/forms are outside this local visual verification.
limitations: Screenshots and input traces require visual review; successful input dispatch is not proof of optical or pixel identity.
RAF cadence measures this headless browser session, not GPU render cost, real-device performance or production frame rate.
Hold/release screenshots exercise the published slowdown input but do not numerically measure its time multiplier.
Mobile/tablet are Chrome viewport, UA and touch emulation, not Safari or real-device tests.
No formal video recording, newsletter submission, external project launch or outbound contact action is performed.

result.verification: Input exercised; review temporal screenshots. Runtime time multiplier is not inferred from RAF.

The collection starts with a visible detail: the shape of a reflection, the path of a card or the response to a gesture. Each experiment follows that detail through its structure, material and timing.
Reference mechanisms are studied carefully, then adapted with Daily Design content. The aim is to make the work observable, understandable and open to further experiments.

SEE ALL STUDIES
Where Interface Details
Become Interactive
Studies
The collection starts with a visible detail: the shape of a reflection, the path of a card or the response to a gesture. Each experiment follows that detail through its structure, material and timing.
Reference mechanisms are studied carefully, then adapted with Daily Design content. The aim is to make the work observable, understandable and open to further experiments.

Existing interface study. Fourteen original graphic studies move through a spatial carousel. Tidal lines, long days and quiet doorways explore typography, reflection and the rhythm of a rotating interface.

Explore the details in these existing captures and concept images. Where a dedicated recording is unavailable, previously recorded Gallery or Orbit experiments provide the motion reference. Original capture and artwork sources are recorded with the study.
